title: Understanding Constant Models
text: A constant model predicts the same value for all inputs. This means that the prediction does not change regardless of the input data.

title: Mean Absolute Error (MAE)
text: MAE is calculated as the average of the absolute differences between the predicted values and the actual values. It is less sensitive to outliers compared to MSE.

title: Mean Squared Error (MSE)
text: MSE is calculated as the average of the squared differences between the predicted values and the actual values. It is more sensitive to outliers compared to MAE.

title: Optimal MAE with Constant Models
text: When using a constant model, the optimal MAE is achieved when the constant prediction is the median of the actual values.

title: Multiple Optimal MAE Values
text: If the dataset has an even number of observations, there can be two different constant predictions (the two middle values) that both result in the optimal MAE.
